To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed methods for registering aerial video to reference images that work in a variety of scenarios including: highly oblique views of the scene, low resolution, low contrast, and low signal-to-noise ratio.

1) we present a method for registering video to reference imagery in real time, 2) we demonstrate the ability to register oblique video to reference imagery with high accuracy, and 3) we demonstrate the accuracy of our method on a large dataset of oblique video frames.
we present a method to geo-register highly oblique aerial video in real time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we register a highly-oblique and/or zoomed in aerial image to a reference image?
the following problems: (1) How can we estimate the geo-coordinates of an object observed in a single frame of video?
the development of a system to geo-register video frames to reference imagery, which includes satellite images, terrain maps and rendered views of the terrain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated a method for registering highly oblique aerial imagery to geo-coordinates in real time.
we have presented methods for registering video frames to a reference map using only a few reference points and that the methods work well for highly oblique imagery and for zoomed in imagery.

the methods presented in this thesis are a significant step forward towards achieving the vision of the DARPA Urban Grand Challenge, where an autonomous ground vehicle will be able to navigate through an urban environment with minimal human intervention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our methods can register video imagery to geo-coordinates with a precision that is on the order of 1-10 meters, depending on the quality and resolution of the video.
we are able to achieve sub-meter geo-accuracy for video imagery with 20 degrees of tilt and 10X zoom.
we have developed a robust and accurate method for registering highly oblique video in real time to a map of the scene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of reference imagery and real-time registration is a powerful tool for geo-locating objects observed in aerial video.
we show that it is possible to register highly oblique video to a reference map in real time with high precision.
we can achieve very precise geo-locations of objects in video even under conditions of severe occlusion, zooming, and oblique views.
